add.k: An older Widow who made an antidote gas in secret
st: In Morocco, Yelena's team hunts Oksana for her antidote gas; stabbed, she frees Yelena with it and tells her to free the others.

files.notes: Named on screen when Yelena, freed, gasps 'Oksana' (transcript). Yelena later says the counteragent was made in secret by an older Widow from Melina's generation, so she was trained in the Red Room; by the film she has gone rogue, and no new group is named on screen, so her last stage is Independent (the wiki's 'unknown organization' is unnamed). Morocco follows the existing Widows file and Wikipedia's filming notes (Tangier); the place is not said in the dialogue.

add.k: An agent who guards President Ross
st: Agent Taylor guards President Ross from the White House summit to Celestial Island, then opens fire when he turns into a red Hulk.

files.notes: Only 'Agent Taylor' is said ('Agent Taylor, you too.', 'Taylor!', 'Agent Taylor?'); 'Leila' is never said in the dialogue, so n is 'Agent Taylor'. She is a Secret Service agent per the wiki and Wikipedia, but 'Secret Service' is not said in the transcript; she serves the President at the White House, so tm uses the app's existing 'The White House' group. Opening fire on the red Hulk and helping pull Sam from the rubble follow the MCU wiki.

st: Ozaki accuses Ross of stealing Japan's adamantium and sends his navy to Celestial Island, but Japan later upholds the treaty.

files.notes: Named on screen ('Prime Minister Ozaki', 'Ozaki and I go back a long way'). Not a villain: he is manipulated by Sterns's leaks, so a Compound file. tm 'Japan' is the nation he leads, said on screen ('Japan wants no part in it'), in the way the app uses 'Wakanda'; switch to 'Independent' if the app prefers not to use a nation for a head of government. Japan upholding the treaty is said at the end ('Japan decided to uphold the treaty').

add.k: An Army recruit Phillips wants made a super soldier
st: Recruit Gilmore Hodge mocks Agent Carter, who knocks him down, then dives from a dummy grenade that Steve throws himself on.

files.notes: Names himself on screen ('Gilmore Hodge, Your Majesty'), and Phillips says 'Hodge passed every test we gave him.' He says he signed up for the U.S. Army. Diving for cover from the grenade follows the MCU wiki; the transcript has only 'Grenade! Get away! Get back!'.

stages.title: Black Widow
stages.text: Under Dreykov's control, Yelena hunts Oksana in Morocco for the antidote gas and stabs her. Dying, Oksana sprays Yelena with the gas, freeing her, and tells her to free the others.
stages.whoA: The Widow who kills her and is freed by her
stages.whoB: The older Widow she kills, who frees her

stages.title: Black Widow
stages.text: Yelena leads a team of Widows in Morocco to take the antidote gas from Oksana, who sets off smoke and flees on foot. After Oksana dies, the team reports Yelena as a deserter.
stages.whoA: The Widows sent to take her antidote gas
stages.whoB: The older Widow whose antidote gas they hunt

stages.title: Captain America: Brave New World
stages.text: Agent Taylor guards President Ross at the White House summit, on his flight to Tokyo, where he orders her to get him to the Indian Ocean within the hour, and at Celestial Island. When Ross turns into a red Hulk at the Rose Garden, she opens fire on him.

stages.title: Captain America: Brave New World
stages.text: Taylor brings Sam to Ross at the White House summit and tells him to keep an open mind. When the red Hulk buries Sam in rubble, she helps Ruth pull him out.
stages.whoA: Captain America, whom she brings to Ross

stages.title: Captain America: Brave New World
stages.text: Taylor and Ruth both serve President Ross. When the red Hulk knocks Sam into the rubble at the White House, the two of them pull him free together.
stages.whoA: Ross's adviser, who helps her rescue Sam

stages.title: Captain America: Brave New World
stages.text: Ross, who says he and Ozaki go back a long way, greets him at the White House summit, but Japan pulls out of the treaty after the attack there. In Tokyo, Ozaki accuses Ross of stealing Japan's adamantium, and over Celestial Island he refuses to believe the American pilots went rogue.
stages.whoA: The US President he blames for the theft

stages.title: Captain America: Brave New World
stages.text: Ross introduces Sam to Ozaki at the White House summit, and the two pose for a photo together. Later, Sam stops the rogue American pilots firing on Japan's fleet.
stages.whoA: Captain America, met at the summit
stages.whoB: Japan's prime minister, met at the summit

stages.title: Captain America: The First Avenger
stages.text: Hodge and Steve are both recruits at Camp Lehigh, and Hodge is Phillips' favorite. When Phillips throws a dummy grenade, Hodge dives for cover while Steve throws himself on it.
stages.whoA: The skinny recruit picked over him
stages.whoB: The bully Phillips wanted to pick

stages.title: Captain America: The First Avenger
stages.text: Hodge mocks Agent Carter's accent and makes a crude pass at her in front of the recruits. She has him step forward and knocks him to the ground.
stages.whoA: The officer who knocks him down

stages.title: Captain America: The First Avenger
stages.text: Phillips backs Hodge as his choice, saying he passed every test, is big and fast and obeys orders. Phillips' dummy grenade test ends up proving Steve the better man instead.
stages.whoA: The colonel who wants him chosen

dropped.why: His name is never said in the dialogue of Captain America: Civil War (he is only the faculty member asking Tony about the grant) or Ironheart episode 1 (Dean Choi does the talking; 'Professor Wilkes' appears only in the subtitles' speaker labels). No nameplate or other on-screen text with his name is evident; credits only.

Not named in the dialogue of Captain America: The First Avenger (transcript has no 'Jones' or 'Gabe'; he only mentions 'three semesters at Howard'). His later appearances are unlabeled photos and the Smithsonian mural in The Winter Soldier, which shows no names (screenshot checked); credits only. The Howling Commandos group file stays.

Not named in the dialogue of Captain America: The First Avenger (no 'Dernier', 'Jacques' or 'Frenchie' in the transcript), and the later photos and Smithsonian mural show no names; credits only. The Howling Commandos group file stays.

Not named in the dialogue of Captain America: The First Avenger (no 'Falsworth' or 'Monty' in the transcript; he only says 'Get this thing going, Dugan!'), and the later photos, Smithsonian mural and Deadpool & Wolverine footage show no name; credits only. The Howling Commandos group file stays.

The drill sergeant is never named in the dialogue of Captain America: The First Avenger ('Rogers! I said fall in!', 'Nobody's got that flag in 17 years!') or The Winter Soldier, and no on-screen text names him; credits only.

'Singh' is never said in Captain America: The Winter Soldier; he is addressed only as 'Councilman' ('For the record, Councilman, he's Algerian'). The Council's hologram booths and the security badges show no names (screenshots checked); credits only.

changes.where: tie Agent Taylor|Thaddeus Ross, Captain America: Brave New World, text
changes.was: Agent Taylor guards President Ross at the White House summit, on his flight to Tokyo and at Celestial Island, where he orders her to get him there within the hour. When Ross turns into a red Hulk at the Rose Garden, she opens fire on him.
changes.now: Agent Taylor guards President Ross at the White House summit, on his flight to Tokyo, where he orders her to get him to the Indian Ocean within the hour, and at Celestial Island. When Ross turns into a red Hulk at the Rose Garden, she opens fire on him.
changes.why: Ross gives the 'within the hour' order in Tokyo, after the treaty talks fail ('Taylor! I want to be en route to the Indian Ocean within the hour'), not at Celestial Island.
